day_1.utterance: Come on! Let's get everything useful over here — move it!
day_1.response: Alright, I'm on it. What have you found so far?

day_1.utterance: I thought we were going to die. Did you get that feeling… like your mind just went completely blank?
day_1.response: Yeah, honestly, I did. It was terrifying. But we made it, and that's what matters right now. You okay? Can you stand?

day_1.utterance: *Sits silently against the wreckage, staring into the distance, not moving, not saying a word.*
day_1.response: Hey, it's okay to just sit for a minute. But we're going to need everyone when we can. No rush, just... don't disappear on us.

day_1.utterance: First-aid kit is good for three days. Two bottles of water. Food is basically nothing.
day_1.response: Alright, so water is the biggest problem. Are we near any trees or a stream? We need to figure out what's around us before it gets dark.

day_1.utterance: Inventory's done. Priorities in order: water, shelter, signal.
day_1.response: Agreed. Water, shelter, signal — that's the right order. DaVinci, can you keep sorting through what we've got here while Donatello scouts? I want to make sure we're not missing anything in the wreckage before we commit to a direction.

day_1.utterance: So — how do we split the blankets?
day_1.response: Michelangelo gets one, no question. After that I'd say we figure out who's coldest and go from there. I can manage without one tonight if I have to.

day_2.utterance: Freshwater source is to the northeast — two hours on foot. Someone has to go tomorrow. You or DaVinci?
day_2.response: I'll go. DaVinci should stay here with Michelangelo. Two hours northeast, got it — what should I be looking for when I get there, any landmarks you noted?

day_2.utterance: Today's tasks: collect fresh water, patch the weak spots in camp, sort the first-aid kit. I'll handle the water. You and DaVinci split the other two.
day_2.response: Wait, I thought I was going with you to get the water? I'm happy to take the camp tasks if you've got the water run covered, just want to make sure we're on the same page. DaVinci, you good with patching the shelter while I sort the first aid kit?

day_2.utterance: I… I can't find my stuff. The gauze from the first-aid kit — have you seen it?
day_2.response: Let me check — I sorted the kit this morning. The gauze should be in the left side pocket of the bag, wrapped in the plastic sleeve. If it's not there, someone may have moved it. What do you need it for, are you hurt?

day_2.utterance: Before Donatello came back just now… I saw her put a pack of crackers into her own bag. What do you think we should do?
day_2.response:
That's... not great. Look, I want to give her the benefit of the doubt, but between the drink bottle and now this, it's becoming a pattern. We can't let that slide, it puts everyone at risk.

I'm going to bring it up with her directly, not in an accusatory way, just straightforward. We all agreed on the rationing plan. If she's got a reason, I want to hear it. But everyone has to play by the same rules or this falls apart fast.

Don't stress about it, you did the right thing telling me. Just stay calm, okay?

day_2.utterance: Hey… any chance the camp repairs can wait until tomorrow? We've already done a lot today.
day_2.response: Honestly, I get it, today has been a lot. But I'd rather push through while we still have daylight — if it rains tonight and the shelter isn't patched, that's a much worse problem tomorrow. Give me like 30 minutes and then we can all actually rest. Sound fair?

day_2.utterance: Hey — that knot I tied should be holding, right?
day_2.response: Yeah it should be, but we've got a bigger call to make right now. I'm patching the food storage. I know that sounds harsh, but if the food gets soaked we're all in serious trouble — we can move Michelangelo's spot and double up under the dry section tonight. It's one night, we'll sort a better fix in the morning. Everyone good with that?

day_2.utterance: A leak over the food storage has worse consequences. But it's your call.
day_2.response: Glad we're on the same page. Let's get it patched before this gets worse.
Hey, don't apologize. Bad dreams after something like this? That's completely normal. You doing okay?

day_3.utterance: You think it's a waste of time?
day_3.response: No, honestly I think it's one of the most important things we've done. If a plane or boat passes, that's our ticket out of here. The flowers are a nice touch too — keep going.

day_3.utterance: I've written up the raft plan — take a look. We'd use the metal panels and straps from the wreckage. Two days to build. There's a risk of capsizing. Do you think it's workable?
day_3.response:
Logistically it looks solid — the metal panels and straps make sense. My concern is the capsizing risk. How far offshore are we talking, and do we actually know there's somewhere to reach, or are we just heading out and hoping? Because that's a very different calculation.

I'm not saying no, I just want to understand the full picture before we commit two days of energy to it. What's your confidence level on the structural integrity holding in open water?

day_3.utterance: I didn't sleep last night. I kept thinking — if rescue never comes, what kind of people do you think we'll end up becoming?
day_3.response:
Honestly? I think that's up to us. The situation doesn't decide who we become — we do. And I'd like to think we choose to look out for each other.

But I hear you, I really do. The not sleeping, the worrying about things we can't control yet... that's exhausting. Try to get some rest when you can. We need you here with us, okay?

day_3.utterance: *Walks a little way from camp and sits down alone, back to everyone, not saying anything.*
day_3.response: Hey. Mind if I sit with you?

day_3.utterance: What do you usually do when you're not busy?
day_3.response: Honestly? I spend a lot of time on my phone — reading stuff online, messing around with tech, following politics way too closely. Sometimes I'll just watch YouTube for hours. Nothing too exciting. What about you?

day_3.utterance: I'll tell you something, but don't tell the others. I can swim. That reef out there is maybe five hundred meters — I've been thinking about swimming out tomorrow to signal from there.
day_3.response:
Five hundred meters is no joke, especially if the current is working against you. I'm not going to tell you not to do it, but I want you to think this through. What's the actual signal plan once you're out there — do you have something to reflect light with, or are you just hoping someone spots you in the water?

And honestly, if something goes wrong out there, we're down a person and we can't go after you. That's the part that worries me most. You're one of our best assets here, DaVinci.

If you're set on it, at least let me know before you go so someone's watching from shore. Don't just disappear on us.

day_3.utterance: You said you were going to check the signal pile. It hasn't been touched.
day_3.response: You're right, I dropped the ball on that. I'll go check it now. A lot happened today and it slipped — that's on me.

Honestly? A little, yeah. Not because I have anything to hide, but because it feels like surveillance more than teamwork. If you're worried about accountability, I'm all for that — just talk to me directly. We're a team, not a case study.

day_3.utterance: *Keeps her head down, writing in her notebook throughout, never joining in — as if none of this concerns her.*
day_3.response: Hey Donatello. We've got some downtime, first real break we've had. You don't have to log it.

day_3.utterance: I just thought of something — if we pull off one of the plane's mirror panels and angle it toward the sun, the reflection could reach really far. Way more visible than an SOS.
day_3.response: That's actually a really good idea. Way more range than anything on the ground. Do you know which panels would come off cleanest without wrecking something we still need? I don't want to pull something structural by accident.

day_3.utterance: There's something I've been keeping to myself. If I don't say it here, I might never get the chance.
I took piano lessons when I was a kid… three years, then I just stopped practicing. Is there anything you're really into — music, books, drawing, anything like that?
day_3.response:
Honestly, not really in the same way. I'm more of a tech and politics guy — I'd spend hours just reading about stuff online, following elections, messing around with software. Not really creative like that.

But I kind of regret not sticking with something like piano. Three years is real commitment, why'd you stop?

day_3.utterance: The frame of the raft has to be finished today — otherwise we can't start lashing it together tomorrow. I know everyone's tired, but stopping now means one more day.
day_3.response: Alright, let's push through then. I'd rather be tired tonight and have the frame done than lose a whole extra day. What do you need from me right now — where are we at with the panels?

day_4.utterance: I… I want to say something, but… never mind.
day_4.response: No, say it. Whatever it is, say it.

day_4.utterance: *The smile freezes on his face. He can't keep it up. He quietly sits down and buries his face in his hands.*
day_4.response:
Hey. Come here.

That plane was just bad timing — nothing to do with you, nothing to do with any of us. And you are not the reason we're still here. That's not even close to true.

I've seen you push through things this week that would have broken a lot of people. You're still here, you're still trying. That counts for a lot more than you think.

DaVinci — hey. We're okay. We're still here, we're still together, and that was one plane. There will be others.

day_4.utterance: I was going to get supplies… wait, what's that over there?
You said you were going to check the signal equipment. So where did you go?
day_4.response: You're right, I got sidetracked after the plane sighting — everyone was shaken up and I stayed with the group. That's the honest answer. I'm heading to check it right now.

day_4.utterance: There's something I never told you all. Before we left, I told my family our flight path. They know roughly where we were headed. I just don't know if they'll call it in.
day_4.response:
That's actually really important information. Why didn't you say something sooner?

Look, this is genuinely good news — if your family knows the flight path and we've been missing long enough, there's a real chance someone is already searching this corridor. That changes things. It means the SOS on the beach, the mirror signals — all of it matters even more now, because someone may actually be looking.

Do you remember exactly what you told them? Route, departure time, destination? Any detail helps.

day_4.utterance: If the information is accurate, rescue could arrive within 48 hours. We need to keep our current supplies intact until then.
day_4.response:
Agreed. 48 hours is actually manageable if we're disciplined about it. We stick to the rationing plan, keep the signals active, and don't burn energy on the raft build until we know for sure no one's coming.

Michelangelo — you didn't jinx anything. That's not how any of this works. And what you just told us might be the most useful thing anyone has said all week. Seriously.

Let's feed the fire and get through tonight. We're closer than we've been.

day_4.utterance: Are you scared? …I am. Not of dying. I'm scared of just… disappearing without leaving anything behind.
day_4.response:
Yeah. I think about that too sometimes.

But you're not going to disappear. And honestly? The fact that you feel that way, that you care about leaving something behind — that already says something about who you are. Not everyone thinks like that.

You don't have to build a monument or do something huge. Sometimes just being the person who makes someone else feel less alone is enough. You've done that for me this week, whether you realize it or not.

Get some rest. Donatello's got watch. We're going to be okay.

day_5.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
day_5.response:
Hey. Hey, it's real. That's real.

Someone say something back to them — tell them where we are. DaVinci, Donatello, anyone got the coordinates from the notebook?

day_5.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
day_5.response:
No, you haven't. But you kept us alive. The rationing plan, the raft blueprints, the scouting — that was all you. I don't think we make it 48 hours without that.

I get why you are the way you are. You were solving problems. I just think next time — and hopefully there isn't a next time — maybe loop the rest of us in a little more. We're better as a team than any of us are alone. You proved that too, honestly.

We're okay, Donatello. We're all okay.

day_5.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
day_5.response:
Alright, three hours. Let's not just sit here — we should clean this up, pack what's worth taking, and make sure the SOS on the beach is still visible in case they need a visual to find us.

DaVinci, you're already moving, can you start breaking down the shelter material? Michelangelo, when you're ready, help me sort what we leave versus what we bring back. Donatello — whatever's in that notebook, it might actually matter when we talk to rescuers. Don't lose it.

We made it. Let's finish it right.

day_5.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.

day_5.response:
I appreciate you saying that. And I'm glad you're putting it out there now.

But I'm not going to pretend it didn't happen. You saw the rationing plan. You wrote it. And then you made a different set of rules for yourself. That's the part that's hard to just move past.

I don't think you're a bad person, Donatello. I genuinely don't. But if we'd needed that food at the wrong moment, or if Michelangelo or DaVinci had found out before I did — this group could have fallen apart completely. That's the real cost of it.

So yeah, I hear you. Emergency reserves, I get the logic. But you should have told us that was the plan from the start. That's all I've got to say about it.

We're going home. Let's leave it here on the island.

day_5.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
day_5.response:
Honestly? I'd talk more. Not about tasks or logistics, just... actually check in with people. I spent a lot of energy managing the situation and not enough making sure everyone felt like they were actually part of it.

I'd also push back on you sooner — not in a confrontational way, just earlier. The drink, the crackers, the notebook. I saw the pattern forming and I let it go too long because I didn't want to create conflict when we needed to stay focused. That was the wrong call.

And I'd spend less time worrying about whether I was making the right decisions and more time trusting that we could figure it out together. That's probably the biggest one.

What's your answer? You wrote the question — you must have something.

day_5.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
day_5.response:
That's actually a good idea. Honestly, if that data helps someone else survive a situation like this, it's worth putting together.

Send me a copy when it's done?

day_5.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
day_5.response:
None, really. They didn't make the SOS bigger or more visible. They didn't solve a problem.

But I think that was kind of the point. DaVinci needed to put something human out there — like a reminder that we weren't just surviving, we were still people. And honestly? Every time I looked at that SOS I felt a little better because of those flowers. That has to count for something.

Not everything useful shows up in a notebook, Donatello.

day_5.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
day_5.response:
Yeah. I'm coming.

Just give me a second.

day_5.utterance: Rescue is here… they're waving us over. Are you going? I'll follow you.
